Questions drive the methods

Complex questions.
Connected approaches.

We connect patient observations with cellular maps and computational analysis, then test mechanistic hypotheses through functional experiments.

01

Map the heterogeneity

Connect clinical phenotypes with PBMC single-cell RNA-seq, and cross-check observations using flow cytometry and public skin datasets.

Clinical phenotyping · Single-cell · Flow cytometry

Our scientific perspective

From biology to medical devices.
One starting point: skin.

How do time and environment change the skin? How do skin-derived signals connect to the brain? How does inflammation become disease? These questions also guide our work in medical devices and precise outcome assessment.

01 / TIME↗
01
Epigenetic Skin Aging

Epigenetic Skin Aging

We investigate how time and environmental exposure reshape gene regulation and the extracellular matrix in skin.

Questions & publications →
02 / CONNECTION↗
02
Skin–Brain Interaction

Skin–Brain Interaction

We explore how environmental exposure and peripheral signals connect the skin to brain function and systemic physiology.

Questions & publications →
03 / DISEASE↗
03
Inflammatory Skin Disease

Inflammatory Skin Disease

We connect clinical questions in atopic dermatitis and related inflammatory skin diseases with immune-cell states and molecular mechanisms.

Questions & publications →
04 / TECHNOLOGY↗
04
Medical Devices & EBD

Medical Devices & EBD

We study skin changes after energy-based treatments through clinical assessment and quantitative imaging, with the PI’s MBA background adding a perspective on clinical needs and technology use.

Selected research

From questions to discoveries.

All publications ↗

Selected publications and Research Stories feature papers in which Dong Hun Lee is a first or corresponding author, including shared first and corresponding authorship.

2026 · Atopic dermatitis · Complementary methods

From immune-cell maps to questions of function

39-parameter CyTOF, public single-cell datasets, suppression assays and skin-tissue validation investigate OX40⁺ regulatory T cells.

Co-corresponding author collaboration
  • Yong-Hee KimPB Immune Therapeutics Inc · Transplantation Research Institute, Seoul National University Medical Research Center
  • Hyun Je KimDepartment of Microbiology and Immunology, Seoul National University College of Medicine
Allergology International↗
2022 · Epigenetics · Integrative analysis

From integrated data to a testable regulator

Transcriptomes from senescence models and HDAC4 perturbation identified DDIT4 for follow-up gene perturbation experiments.

Co-corresponding author collaboration
  • Daehee HwangDepartment of Biological Sciences, Seoul National University
  • Jin Ho ChungDepartment of Dermatology, Seoul National University College of Medicine
Aging↗
Beyond the skin
2024 · Skin–brain axis · Animal study

Connecting cutaneous UV exposure and memory

Animal studies examined how chronic UV exposure relates to dopamine signaling, memory and synaptic function.

Co-corresponding author collaboration
  • Jin Ho ChungDepartment of Dermatology, Seoul National University Hospital, Seoul National University College of Medicine

Experimental & Molecular Medicine↗

Article titles link to the original publications. Animal-model findings do not establish clinical effects in humans.
